title: Scary Movie 4
synopsis: Aliens. Ghosts. A grim village. A hand reaching out of the well. Also somebody on a unicycle for no reason. Welcome to the parody — pick the dumbest possible choice and probably live.

nodes.text: An ominous tripod legs over your fence. Your neighbor Tom screams artistically. A baby in a stroller deadlifts a chainsaw. You're holding a TV remote and a half-eaten waffle.

choices.consequence: Absurdity is a shield in this universe.

nodes.text: You hide in the basement, which has, inexplicably, a karaoke machine and three life-size mannequins of yourself. One of them is doing your taxes.
You sprint and accidentally arrive in a black-and-white village from a completely different horror movie. The elders look at you suspiciously. There is a strict no-shoes policy.

choices.consequence: When in spoof, do as the spoof does.

nodes.text: Brenda is hiding from a ghost-cousin and watching the news, which is just a guy in glasses yelling about cats. The ghost rises from her TV in 480i resolution.

choices.text: Negotiate with the ghost about residuals
choices.consequence: “Negotiate with the ghost about residuals” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Hollywood logic.

nodes.text: Tom Ryan is operating a crane while being chased by a swarm of polite swarming birds. He keeps yelling at his son — who is actually a thirty-five-year-old man wearing a propeller hat.

choices.text: Stay on the ground and yell back

nodes.text: Mayor Baxter convenes an emergency meeting. The agenda includes alien invasion, a strange smell, and Mrs. Peterson's cat being on Roomba again.

choices.text: Propose dancing as a global defense

choices.consequence: “Propose hiding under the table” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Underrated tactic.

nodes.text: An iron lung patient — played by a celebrity in a horrendous prosthetic — hands you a clue: 'The aliens hate French music. Trust me.'
A massive alien tripod strides through Main Street. The driver inside is a small alien wearing oven mitts. He waves apologetically as he steps on a hot dog cart.

choices.text: Throw a banana peel under the tripod

nodes.text: A girl with wet hair crawls out of a well. She's just looking for Wi-Fi. The router has been on the fritz since the 1800s.

choices.text: Help her connect to your hotspot
Push her gently back in the well
choices.consequence: You commit to “Push her gently back in the well.” The story records the instinct as “Reasonable boundaries” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You and Brenda end up in a cell with the President, who is currently in a Catholic school reading a children's book about ducks. He refuses to leave until the duck book is finished.

choices.text: Read the duck book aloud to expedite

nodes.text: You wake in a filthy bathroom chained to a sink. A puppet on a tricycle informs you that you have to choose between sawing off your own leg or assembling IKEA furniture without instructions.

choices.text: Pretend to saw and bluff the puppet
choices.consequence: “Pretend to saw and bluff the puppet” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Performative compliance.

nodes.text: You appear, somehow, on Oprah's set. She jumps on the couch demanding you announce your love for someone. You don't know who. The audience cheers regardless.

choices.text: Profess love for the iron-lung patient
choices.consequence: Plot twist for the awards reel.

nodes.text: A car chase through suburbia somehow involves three weddings, a marching band, and Charlie Sheen's face on every billboard. You're driving with your knees and texting with your eyebrows.

choices.text: Use the marching band as a roadblock
Crash the wedding to slow down the bad guy
choices.consequence: “Crash the wedding to slow down the bad guy” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Romcom physics.

nodes.text: The aliens, it turns out, are scared of love. Brenda and you, holding hands while delivering a monologue, are functionally a nuke. The tripod tilts toward you, weeping politely.
You're absorbed into the tripod. Inside, it's a Costco. The aliens are buying bulk humans for snacks. You sneak into the sample aisle as a disguise.

choices.text: Sample your way to the controls
Convince the aliens to give up snacks for Lent

nodes.text: Brenda gives a Best Original Speech that makes the aliens cry chrome tears. The tripods all sit down in formation. Earth's anthem plays through three different car alarms.
Tom Ryan, despite being absolutely no good at parenting, manages to defeat the lead alien by accident with a beer bong and a leaf blower. His son slow-claps with the propeller hat still spinning.

choices.text: Steal the credit on live TV
choices.consequence: Karma takes a sick day in spoofs.

nodes.text: The threat is over. A second tripod ominously rises behind you. Then a third. Then a fourth, which is just a person on stilts who's late to the bit.

choices.consequence: “Run for a sequel hook” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Studio mandate.

nodes.text: A famous-but-unnamed celebrity stops the scene to demand a cameo. They've heard the residuals are good. You allow it because they brought their own catering.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Tradition—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Let the boom mic do the closer

nodes.text: The credits roll over outtakes of you tripping into a wedding cake. Audiences laugh. Critics will be furious. Studio sets a release date for Scary Movie 5 before the lights come up.

choices.text: Slip out the back of the cinema

nodes.text: You and Brenda, three years later, are at a kids' birthday party. The clown is, suspiciously, an alien in a hat. Nobody is paying attention. You smile, because that's the joke.

choices.text: Eat cake and ignore the alien
choices.consequence: Be the calm in the spoof.

nodes.text: The credits roll on you and Brenda waving from a parade float made of taxi roof signs. Critics call it 'the dumbest defeat of evil in cinema history,' which the marketing team prints on the poster verbatim.
Brenda is sworn in. Her first executive order is mandatory karaoke Tuesdays. Approval ratings hit 93%. The aliens write a strongly-worded letter and then visit on vacation.
Tom is celebrated worldwide for accidentally winning a war. He sells autographs at fairs. His son finally takes off the propeller hat. You are happy for them in a slightly bewildered way.
You take the credit on live TV. Within six minutes you're trending for the wrong reasons. Your reputation is repaired only after a heartfelt podcast apology and a charity bake sale.
A title card promises 'Scary Movie 5: This Time It's Personal-er.' Nobody asked. Everyone shows up anyway. Spoofs, like cockroaches, survive everything.
You walk into the sunset which is, on closer inspection, a painted sheet held up by two stagehands. One of them shrugs. You shrug back. Roll credits.
